::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this chapter does

Use this chapter when changing Stata code, Quarto source, Python support code, configuration or another maintained project file.

The aim is to make mistakes **small, visible and reversible**.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Procedure at a glance"}
1. Update local `main` and create a focused development branch.
2. Make the smallest useful source change.
3. Inspect the exact difference and test every affected pathway.
4. Review the result, commit and push the branch.
5. Merge through a pull request and check the resulting workflow or website.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Do not test by editing generated outputs

Do not experiment by editing a generated dataset, public CSV or workbook, `approval.yml`, `public_manifest.csv`, published figure or `site/_site/`.

Correct the authoritative data, reference data, configuration or source code and rerun.
:::

## Before you start

Define the problem, the files expected to change, the workflows that may be affected and what a successful test should show.

If the change affects an approved method, disclosure control, approval or publication rules, public output structure, required software or staff responsibilities, agree the intended change with the BNR Lead before coding it.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Input files

| File or source | What to check |
|---|---|
| Maintained source file to be changed | It owns the behaviour that needs correction; it is not a generated output or disposable website copy. |
| Current callers, dialogs, help and manual pages | Identify every route that depends on the changed file, especially before changing a shared helper. |
| Existing test, synthetic fixture or previous expected result | It provides an appropriate comparison for the affected pathway. |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code and configuration files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| The selected tracked Stata, QMD, Python, PowerShell, batch or configuration source | Edit directly on the development branch. |
| `.gitignore` | Protects local configuration, virtual environments, private material and generated output. Change only when the storage policy genuinely changes. |
| `scripts/stata/README.qmd` | Current Stata entry points and maintenance rules; update when a Stata responsibility or dependency materially changes. |
| `docs/bnr-refit-project-guiderails.md` | Project architecture and change-control boundary; update only for a material operating-model or architecture change. |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Outputs and evidence

| File or result | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Relevant workflow test, review package or full Quarto render | Shows whether the affected pathway still behaves correctly. Keep private evidence outside Git where required. |
| Git diff and focused commit | Record the reviewed source change without unrelated edits. |
| GitHub development branch and pull request | Provide the review and protected-`main` merge route. |
:::

## Step 1: Start from an up-to-date `main`

In VS Code:

1. Open **Source Control**.
2. Check that there are no unexplained local changes.
3. Click the branch name in the lower-left status bar and select `main`.
4. Select **Source Control > ... > Pull**.

If `main` contains local changes you do not understand, stop and identify them before pulling.

The equivalent commands, entered in a **VS Code PowerShell terminal**, are:

```powershell
git status
git switch main
git pull origin main
```

`git status` should show a clean working tree, and the pull should complete without a merge conflict.

## Step 2: Create a focused development branch

In VS Code:

1. click the branch name;
2. select **Create new branch**; and
3. enter a short descriptive name, such as `fix-table-label` or `update-python-dependency`.

The equivalent command is:

```powershell
git switch -c fix-table-label
```

Replace the example name. The command should report that Git switched to the new branch. Do not make routine changes directly on `main`.

## Step 3: Choose the required test scope

Use the smallest test that gives reasonable confidence, but test every current caller of a changed shared helper.

| Change | Minimum test |
|---|---|
| QMD wording, link or layout | Local preview, local-link check and complete `quarto render` |
| Annual report analyst module | Build the candidate and review every affected output |
| Dashboard or table presentation | Complete render and inspection against its approved public data |
| Product-specific Stata calculation | Run from the earliest affected product step and inspect its quality and review outputs |
| Shared Stata helper | Test every current workflow that calls it |
| Menu, dialog or help | Open the entry point and run the affected route |
| Path or setup | Repeat the relevant [workstation checks](../getting-started/workstation-setup.qmd) |
| Python dependency or support code | Run the environment check, affected utility and complete Quarto render |
| Disclosure, approval or publication control | Test the full affected control pathway with suitable non-confidential test data |

## Step 4: Make the smallest useful change

- Avoid unrelated cleanup and unnecessary renaming.
- Avoid new dependencies when the existing tools can do the job.
- Keep Stata readable for mixed-skill analysts.
- Keep analytical calculations in Stata and presentation in Quarto.
- Keep analytical decisions visible in analyst-owned or metric-specific DO files.
- Update dependent dialogs, help files, and authoritative manual pages in the same controlled change.

## Step 5: Inspect the difference

In VS Code Source Control, open each changed file and read the before-and-after comparison.

Check that only intended lines changed, no credentials or private paths were added, temporary files are absent and formatting changes have not obscured the substantive change.

Equivalent commands:

```powershell
git status
git diff --check
git diff
```

## Step 6: Run and review the required tests

For an analytical pathway:

1. rerun from the earliest affected step;
2. read the final Stata summary and private log;
3. inspect the quality and review outputs;
4. compare the result with an appropriate expected or previous result; and
5. complete human review before any approval or public promotion.

A successful Stata run does not prove that the result is correct.

For a complete Quarto render, enter in a VS Code PowerShell terminal at the repository root:

```powershell
.\venv-info-hub\Scripts\Activate.ps1
cd site
quarto render
```

Inspect the affected pages, neighbouring navigation and any changed listing or download.

## Step 7: Check the complete Git change

Before committing, confirm that:

- only intended files changed;
- no confidential or private file is listed;
- `bnr_paths_LOCAL.do`, `venv-info-hub/` and `site/_site/` are not in the *VS Code* Source Control list;
- approved outputs changed only through the controlled workflow; and
- temporary test files are also not in the *VS Code* Source Control list.

Use [System reference](../reference/index.qmd) if you do not recognise a file.

## Step 8: Commit and push

In VS Code Source Control:

1. stage only the intended files;
2. enter a short commit message;
3. select **Commit**; and
4. select **Publish Branch** or **Push**.

Equivalent commands:

```powershell
git add path/to/changed-file
git commit -m "Fix table period label"
git push -u origin fix-table-label
```

Replace the path, message and branch name. The push should report the remote branch and normally provide a pull-request link.

## Step 9: Review and merge

On GitHub, create a pull request from the development branch to `main`.

Before merging, review the changed-file list, confirm the required tests passed, confirm the result still matches the task and obtain BNR review for any material method or governance change.

Merge through the pull request. Do not push directly to protected `main`. If the change affects the website, confirm the **Publish Quarto site** action and inspect the live result.

## Step 10: Update material documentation

Git records the implementation history. Update an authoritative document only when the change materially affects the operating model, method, control, dependency or responsibility.

| Change | Documentation to consider |
|---|---|
| Stata responsibility, entry point or dependency | `scripts/stata/README.qmd` and the affected Technical page |
| Operating model, architecture, role or product structure | `docs/bnr-refit-project-guiderails.md` |
| Operator decision or authority | The relevant Operations Manual page |
| Public measure or interpretation | The relevant Public Methods Manual page |

Routine data releases and minor wording changes need no separate changelog.

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## If the change does not complete safely

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Wrong edit, not committed | In VS Code, discard only the confirmed file change; equivalent: `git restore path/to/file`. |
| Wrong branch commit | Prefer a corrective commit or abandon the branch. Do not rewrite `main` history. |
| Problem found after merge | Create a correction branch from current `main`, correct the source, retest and merge normally. |
| Public analytical output is affected | Correct it through the controlled analytical workflow; never hand-edit the live file. |
| Merge conflict or methodological answer is unclear | Stop and obtain help before accepting either version or continuing. |
| Confidential material may have entered Git | Stop sharing and follow the security-incident guidance in [Fix common problems](troubleshooting.qmd#git-problems). |
:::
